newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African '97 growth one pct but rand strong - fund.
newsitem.headline: S.African '97 growth one pct but rand strong - fund.

text.p: South Africa's economic growth is likely to slow materially to around one percent in 1997 but the rand could show surprising strength, RMB Fund Managers said in an economic overview published on Wednesday.
RMB's growth prediction is considerably lower than most economists' expectations of 2.0-2.5 percent, down from 3.0 percent in 1996.
It said the sharp slowdown was a reflection of the heavy toll that high interest rates would take on the economy.

Maintaining high interest rates remains a cornerstone of the authorities' fight against inflation and consequently it was unlikely that the central Reserve bank would contemplate a significant easing before the second half of 1997.
The rand, however, should be a success story in 1997 after its 28 percent plunge against the dollar in 1996.

"The fundamentals suggest that the current value of the rand against all major currencies represents an undershoot from which level it could show surpising strength similar to its performance in the middle 1980s," RMB Fund Managers said.
The currency would be supported by improved capital inflows and a better current acount balance.

RMB said inflation, which stood at 9.2 percent year-on-year in November, was likely to drift moderately higher in the first few months of 1997 on the back of higher food prices and the impact of the weaker rand. But around mid-year it should start moving down again.
South Africa's Bank rate currently stands at 17 percent while commercial banks' prime lending rates are at 20.25 percent.
